docs.title: Coupled Modal Narrative Engine
docs.text:
CMNE Workbench is a local desktop instrument for drafting a bounded fictional scene, tracking what characters and readers can know, and producing an offline prose passage from a discourse plan. It separates story (what happens) from discourse (the order and form in which a reader encounters it). Its Mara and Len sample compares four kinds of change in Mara's understanding.

Implementation scope

This site documents version 0.1.0 as implemented on 2026-10-20. The workbench has a Tauri/React interface and a Python sidecar. The seeded sample can produce four deterministic passages of about 800 words. It has no language-model adapter, blinded study workflow, or complete formal revision engine. Pages mark proposed behavior explicitly.

docs.text: If you want to… Start here Install and run the app Install and launch See the idea in ten minutes First run: Mara and Len Make your own scene Build a scene and constructs and rules Understand the four conditions Revise and compare Get the generated passage Generate and export Interpret a run's status and limits Read the result Extend the Python kernel or sidecar API overview Study architecture and theory Design overview

docs.title: One scene, two orders
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Fixture: actors, objects, initial facts] --> B[Story events: what happens]
    B --> C[Discourse acts: what is told]
    C --> D[Scene packet]
    D --> E[Offline realizer]
    E --> F[Passage and findings]
    B --> G[Six replay projections]
    C --> G
    G --> D

Example. In story time, Len repairs a chair before he leaves. In telling time, the reader meets the rocking chair after he leaves and learns about the repair later. A later event can change Mara's interpretation of that earlier repair without changing the original event.

docs.title: Documentation set
docs.text:
• The user manual is task-based. It follows the numbered scenarios S-01 through S-13 and uses labeled information blocks so a reader can find a procedure, rule, or explanation quickly.
  • The design section explains the implemented state, domain model, processes, storage, and gaps from the target SRS.
  • The API section covers the Python package, CLI, JSON-RPC sidecar, contracts, errors, and Tauri bridge.

The longer target specifications remain in the repository's _design/ folder. This site describes the running application and identifies design goals that have not yet shipped.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The Python kernel is the source of narrative rules. The CLI calls it directly. The desktop UI calls it through Tauri's rpc_call, which relays to a line-framed JSON-RPC sidecar. The sidecar and GUI use the same project storage.

flowchart LR
  CLI --> Kernel[Python cmne kernel]
  React --> Tauri[Tauri rpc_call]
  Tauri --> Sidecar[cmne-sidecar]
  Sidecar --> Kernel
  Kernel --> Files[(Project folder)]
Interface Use Python kernel Scripting and tests in the same Python process CLI Create, run, and inspect a graph from a terminal JSON-RPC Full project, draft, graph, run, and export operations Data contracts Event fields, formula syntax, validation, errors Tauri bridge Frontend to sidecar command boundary

Protocol version is 1.0; project/event schema version is 1. Methods returning errors do not mutate sealed history unless explicitly described. See the storage design for the on-disk model.

docs.title: Command-line interface
docs.text:
Install the package in a virtual environment, then run cmne --help.

Command Effect Output cmne create PATH [--name NAME] [--sample] Create a new project; --sample seeds Mara and Len and C0–C3 Project path cmne run PATH [--branch ID] Synchronously run a branch; default main Pretty printed run JSON cmne graph PATH [--branch ID] [--lens LENS] Read a lens graph; defaults main, story Pretty printed graph JSON 
source .venv/bin/activate
cmne create /tmp/cmne-example --sample
cmne run /tmp/cmne-example --branch main
cmne graph /tmp/cmne-example --branch main --lens story

Accepted lens names are fixture, story, discourse, mind, provenance, motif, and pipeline. For the sample comparison, inspect branch IDs in project.cmne.json or use the GUI/sidecar branch.list. The CLI does not expose export or draft editing; JSON-RPC does.

docs.title: Data contracts and errors
docs.text: All documents are JSON-compatible. IDs are strings. Basis-point values are integers in 0..10000. Validators return a copy with defaults and, for fixture/contract, a content_hash.

docs.title: Fixture and contract
docs.text:
{
  "actors": [{"id":"mara","name":"Mara"},{"id":"len","name":"Len"}],
  "entities": [{"id":"chair","name":"Chair","kind":"object","motif":true}],
  "initial_facts": [],
  "style": {"focalizer":"mara","distance":"close"}
}

A fixture requires exactly two actors, each with unique id and name. Entities need unique IDs and names. Optional initial facts and style feed replay. A new project uses actor_a and actor_b placeholders and no entities.

{
  "required_story_conditions": [],
  "forbidden_story_conditions": [],
  "facts_that_must_be_clear": [],
  "questions_that_must_remain_open": [],
  "prose_bounds": {"min_words":0,"max_words":1100},
  "strain_threshold_bp":6500
}

Required and forbidden conditions may not overlap; a claim may not be both clear and open. Bounds must be ordered nonnegative integers. The current run checks required story facts, forbidden literal prose strings, and word bounds. Other fields are stored for future checks.

docs.title: Story event payload
docs.text:
{
  "title":"Mara finds the note",
  "kind":"observation",
  "description":"A note lies beneath the bowl.",
  "actor_ids":["mara"],
  "entity_ids":["bowl"],
  "causal_parents":["evt_…"],
  "observed_by":["mara"],
  "access_path":"perception",
  "world_facts":["note_under_bowl"],
  "strain_bp":4800,
  "preconditions":[]
}

title is required. kind defaults to action and may be action, observation, utterance, recollection, decision, revision, or crisis. Causal parents must be earlier sealed event IDs. Observation requires observed_by and an access path of perception, testimony, or memory. strain_bp defaults to 0. Optional interpretations have observer_id, positive model_version, claim, and earlier target_story_sequences. Optional belief_revision has observer, claim, accepted/rejected/suspended status, confidence_bp, and an accessible earlier evidence_story_sequence. modal_revision has observer and add_scenarios; conceptual_revision has observer, concepts, and migration_map.

docs.title: Discourse act payload
docs.text:
{
  "title":"The note",
  "mode":"scene",
  "story_refs":["evt_…"],
  "text":"Under the bowl, a folded note waited.",
  "focalizer":"mara",
  "reveal":["note_under_bowl"],
  "cue":[],
  "withhold":[]
}

title is required. mode defaults to scene and also accepts summary, ellipsis, pause, memory, and repetition. References must exist on the branch. Every revealed claim must occur in a referenced event's world_facts, unless hypothetical or unreliable is truthy. A claim already revealed cannot later be withheld. text becomes prose in the offline realizer.

docs.title: Formula AST
docs.text:
{"op":"and","operands":[
  {"op":"atom","predicate":"note_under_bowl"},
  {"op":"believes","observer_id":"mara","operands":[
    {"op":"atom","predicate":"len_left"}
  ]}
]}

Operators: atom, not, and, or, implies, necessarily, possibly, believes, suspends, in_scenario. atom takes predicate as a string or {name, arguments, polarity} object. not, the two modal operators, believes, suspends, and in_scenario take one operand; implies takes two; and/or take 2–16. believes/suspends require observer_id; in_scenario requires scenario_id. Maximum depth is 16 and maximum nodes 256. Evaluation returns true, false, or unknown (None) when the available state cannot decide a claim.

docs.title: Sealed event envelope
docs.text:
{"stream":"story","branch_id":"main","sequence":1,"schema_version":1,
 "payload":{"title":"…"},"event_id":"evt_…","integrity_hash":"…"}

The event ID and integrity hash derive from the canonical envelope body. event_id is a stable prefix of the hash; integrity_hash is the full SHA-256 hex digest. Opening/reading a stream verifies both.

docs.title: Common domain errors
docs.text:
Code Meaning / action E-FIXTURE-001, E-CONTRACT-001 Correct fixture cast/IDs or contract fields E-STORY-001, E-DISCOURSE-001 Correct event/act fields or references E-ACCESS-001 Add observer/access path or accessible belief evidence E-DISCLOSURE-001 Ground a reveal or fix withhold order E-FORMULA-001 Correct a bounded formula AST E-DRAFT-001, E-GRAPH-001 Fix draft fields/edges before seal E-STORE-001, E-SCHEMA-001 Stream failed integrity/schema validation; restore a valid backup E-LOCK-001 Close the other writer before opening the project E-RUN-001, E-EXPORT-001 Match branch/condition or run before export

The sidecar's error.data includes cmne_code, field_path, next_action, and cause for domain errors. command.submit can instead report a rejected command inside a successful RPC result.

docs.title: JSON-RPC sidecar
docs.text:
cmne-sidecar (or python -m cmne_sidecar.server) reads one JSON-RPC 2.0 request per input line and writes one response per output line. Keep one process open for a sequence of calls. app.hello must succeed before other methods; it accepts protocol major version 1 and returns version, schema, package, and lens names. Standard output is protocol only; diagnostics use standard error.

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"app.hello","params":{"protocol_version":"1.0"}}

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocol_version":"1.0","schema_version":1,"package_version":"…","lenses":["fixture","story","discourse","mind","provenance","motif","pipeline"]}}

docs.title: Project and validation
docs.text:
Method Parameters Result project.create path required; name, sample optional Project summary project.sample Optional path; defaults to Documents/CMNE/Mara and Len Opens or seeds sample; summary project.open path Project summary project.close — { "closed": true } project.get — Project summary fixture.validate / contract.validate fixture / contract Validated object with content_hash; no open project required fixture.get / contract.get — Current object fixture.save / contract.save fixture / contract Validated and saved object

The summary has path, name, active_branch, branches, fixture, and contract. Saving fixture/contract updates the current project document; it does not rewrite already sealed events.

docs.title: Branch, events, and graph
docs.text:
All branch-aware methods accept optional branch_id; omitted means the metadata's active branch, or main.

Method Other parameters Result branch.list — Branch metadata array branch.fork sequence required; name optional New branch_id, fork_sequence, draft_id branch.compare left, right Shared prefix, first divergence, unique counts, hashes events.read stream optional, default story Verified event array command.submit stream (story/discourse), payload, optional expected_sequence accepted, emitted_events, rejected_reason, invariant results, before/after hashes graph.get lens, optional draft_id, sequence, discourse_index Lens graph envelope graph.validate_connection lens, source, target, kind, optional draft {accepted, reason} scrub.projection Optional sequence, discourse_index Six projections and hashes overlay.series / strain.series — Tension projection, including series trace.query node_id Causal parents, observers, disclosures, interpretations

command.submit returns accepted: false for a narrative validation rejection rather than an RPC error. Check that field before assuming the event was appended.

docs.title: Drafts
docs.text:
Method Parameters Result draft.create Optional lens (story by default) Empty draft draft.get draft_id Draft JSON draft.patch draft Saved draft JSON draft.compile_preview draft or draft_id {accepted, errors, count} draft.seal draft_id {accepted, errors, emitted_events, id_map} draft.delete draft_id {deleted: true}

A draft contains id, branch_id, lens, nodes, and edges. Node entries have id, title, and fields; edge entries have source, target, and kind (causes for story or refs for discourse). Preview and seal validate references, fields, and graph rules. Story draft seals in causal order; discourse draft seals in node ID order when no causal dependencies exist.

docs.title: Run and export
docs.text:
Method Parameters Result packet.build / packet.get Optional branch_id Current computed packet; these do not read an archived packet by hash run.start Optional branch_id, conditions One run; or {runs, status} for exactly C0,C1,C2,C3 run.status Optional branch_id Latest saved run or idle status run.cancel — {cancelled:false, reason:…} because runs are synchronous export.report Optional branch_id {path} for latest run's Markdown report

For a single run, the condition must match the selected branch's condition. To run all four sample branches, pass conditions: ["C0","C1","C2","C3"] in that order. export.report requires a saved run for that branch.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"…","data":{"cmne_code":"E-STORY-001","field_path":"title","next_action":"…","cause":"…"}}}

-32000 wraps a CmneError; -32602 indicates invalid parameters; -32700 indicates invalid JSON; -32603 is an internal sidecar error. The cmne_code gives the domain-specific cause. Unknown methods yield E-RPC-001. See Data contracts and errors.

docs.title: Python kernel
docs.text:
Install the project in a virtual environment as described in Install and launch. Imports below use the installed cmne package.

from cmne.project import Project

project = Project.create("/tmp/my-scene", "My scene")
try:
    story = project.append_story("main", {
        "title": "The letter arrives",
        "kind": "action",
        "actor_ids": ["actor_a"],
        "description": "A letter arrives at the door."
    })
    project.append_discourse("main", {
        "title": "Opening",
        "mode": "scene",
        "story_refs": [story["event_id"]],
        "text": "A letter waited at the door."
    })
    result = project.run("main")
    print(result["status"], result["prose"])
finally:
    project.close()

docs.title: Project lifecycle and storage
docs.text:
Method Inputs Result Project.create(root, name, sample=False) Empty project path; optional seeded sample Open Project Project(root) Existing project path Open and lock project close() — Releases writer lock branch_ids() — List of branch IDs events(branch, stream) Stream story, discourse, or evaluation Verified event list append_story(branch, payload, expected_sequence=None) Valid story payload Sealed event append_discourse(branch, payload, expected_sequence=None) Valid discourse payload Sealed event projection(branch, sequence=None, discourse_index=None) Optional prefixes projections and hashes fork(branch, sequence, name) Existing branch and story prefix length New branch ID and suffix draft_id compare(left, right) Two branch IDs Shared/diverging counts and hashes

Use expected_sequence for optimistic concurrency on append. Sealed history is verified when read and stored atomically when written.

docs.title: Draft, graph, and run methods
docs.text:
Method Purpose draft_create(branch, lens) Create empty story or discourse draft draft_get(draft_id) / draft_save(draft) Read or replace a draft JSON document draft_preview(draft) / draft_seal(draft_id) Validate and append draft events validate_connection(branch, lens, source, target, kind, draft=None) Check a draft edge graph(lens, branch, draft_id=None, sequence=None, discourse_index=None) Lens graph envelope trace(branch, node_id) Causal/disclosure/interpretation details run(branch, conditions=None) Synchronous run and persisted packet/result list_runs() Saved run records in sequence order

draft_seal returns accepted, errors, emitted_events, and id_map. A rejected preview does not append events. run returns status, prose, findings, stages, packet/projection hashes, and IDs; a failed run is still saved.

docs.title: Pure functions
docs.text:
cmne.core provides validate_fixture, validate_contract, validate_story_event, validate_discourse_act, replay, build_packet, template_realize, check_realization, canonical, digest, and stable_id. cmne.formula provides validate, evaluate, and EvaluationContext. They accept JSON-compatible dictionaries/lists and return JSON-compatible values, except formula evaluation returns True, False, or None. Validation raises CmneError with code, field_path, and next_action; the sidecar serializes it as RPC error data.

These functions are the current Python interfaces, not a separate network service. For the exact field shapes, see Data contracts.

docs.title: Tauri bridge
docs.text:
The Rust shell exposes two commands to the React frontend:

Command Arguments Result rpc_call method: string, params: JSON object Sidecar result value or rejected promise with error string default_sample_path None Documents/CMNE/Mara and Len path 
import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";

const project = await invoke("rpc_call", {
  method: "project.sample",
  params: {},
});
const path = await invoke<string>("default_sample_path");

app/src/api.ts wraps invoke in rpc<T>(method, params) and turns serialized sidecar errors into messages containing the CMNE code and field path. It also defines Lens, ViewNode, ViewEdge, ViewGraph, Draft, ProjectSummary, and RunResult TypeScript types.

The Rust bridge permits only methods in its METHODS allow-list, currently the JSON-RPC reference method set. It owns one child sidecar behind a mutex, increments request IDs, checks matching response IDs, and performs the protocol handshake on start. Development uses python3 -m cmne_sidecar.server with PYTHONPATH set to the repository src; the packaged app uses its bundled cmne-sidecar executable. CMNE_SIDECAR_BIN can override the child path. After an unexpected exit or broken pipe, the bridge starts a new child and retries the call once; clients may need to reopen the project because sidecar state is process-local.

The shell does not interpret narrative payloads. Validation and storage stay in the Python kernel. A single synchronous run blocks the sidecar request until it returns; run.cancel is currently a no-op response.

docs.title: Design overview
docs.text:
CMNE is a local narrative workbench for a bounded two-actor scene. It separates what happened (story) from how the reader encounters it (discourse), then replays sealed events into actor, world, reader, tension, and style views. A scene packet feeds an offline deterministic realizer. The desktop app is Tauri 2, React, and a Python sidecar.

flowchart LR
  Author --> React[React workbench]
  React --> Tauri[Tauri command bridge]
  Tauri --> Python[Python sidecar and kernel]
  Python --> Store[(Local project folder)]
  Python --> Run[Packet, prose, findings]
  Run --> React

The design pages document implemented behavior. The original _design specifications describe the broader research system. See Current limits before treating a research scenario as available in this build.

Topic Page Narrative entities, revisions, and the C0–C3 comparison Domain model Components and protocol boundary Runtime architecture Deterministic run and checking Pipeline Project layout, integrity, and branches Storage Shipped scope and planned work Roadmap

For user tasks, start with the manual. For callable interfaces, see the API.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as React workbench
  participant Shell as Tauri/Rust
  participant RPC as Python sidecar
  participant Kernel as cmne kernel
  participant Files as Project files
  UI->>Shell: invoke rpc_call(method, params)
  Shell->>RPC: one JSON-RPC request line
  RPC->>Kernel: dispatch and validate
  Kernel->>Files: read/write project state
  Kernel-->>RPC: result or CmneError
  RPC-->>Shell: one JSON-RPC response line
  Shell-->>UI: result or error string

The React UI owns editing interaction and graph presentation. The Rust command rpc_call restricts method names and serializes access to one child process. It starts the Python sidecar from the development virtual environment or bundled executable, performs app.hello, and restarts once after a broken pipe. The sidecar speaks line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on standard input/output; logs go to standard error. The Python kernel owns narrative validation, storage, replay, packet construction, realization, and checking.

The UI offers seven lenses. Story and Discourse allow drafts; Fixture, Mind, Provenance, Motif, and Pipeline visualize current or derived data. The graph envelope includes nodes and edges with IDs, titles, fields, state, and text alternatives. An outline, inspector, scrubber, strain chart, trace pane, and branch comparison provide other routes through the same data.

docs.title: Runtime boundaries
docs.text:
Boundary Contract React → Rust Tauri invoke("rpc_call", {method, params}) or default_sample_path Rust → Python One JSON-RPC request/response per newline, protocol major version 1 Sidecar → kernel In-process Python calls over JSON-compatible values Kernel → disk Local project directory, hashed NDJSON streams and atomic JSON writes

The sidecar is stateful: app.hello precedes other calls and one project can be open in a process. The project lock allows one writer. Read the JSON-RPC reference and Tauri bridge for method details.

docs.title: Story, discourse, and perspectives
docs.text:
The fixture names exactly two actors, entities, initial facts, and optional style. The contract states required/forbidden story conditions, facts that should be clear, questions left open, prose bounds, and a strain threshold. Story events are sealed in sequence; discourse acts select and order references to those events. Replay derives six projections: actor_a, actor_b, environment, tension, reader, and prose_style.

erDiagram
  PROJECT ||--|| FIXTURE : contains
  PROJECT ||--|| CONTRACT : contains
  PROJECT ||--o{ BRANCH : contains
  BRANCH ||--o{ STORY_EVENT : seals
  BRANCH ||--o{ DISCOURSE_ACT : seals
  DISCOURSE_ACT }o--o{ STORY_EVENT : references
  STORY_EVENT ||--o{ INTERPRETATION : records
  BRANCH ||--o{ RUN : produces

The sample Mara and Len is a controlled comparison. C0 reveals a fact; C1 revises a belief; C2 adds a possible situation; C3 changes the concepts used to classify prior events. All share the same first seven story events and diverge later. The question is whether a later change affects how earlier details are understood, even though the sealed past stays intact.

Revision Implemented representation Projection effect Interpretation Claim tied to an observer and earlier story sequence(s) Adds an interpretation and belief to that actor Belief Observer, claim, status, confidence, accessible evidence Replaces that actor's claim status Modal Observer and added scenarios Increments modal model version and appends scenarios Conceptual Observer, concepts, migration map Creates a new conceptual model version with superseded model

This representation supports useful inspection, but it is not yet a complete formal epistemic/modal revision engine. The current formula AST supports tri-state preconditions and bounded syntax; provenance and grounding checks are partial.

docs.title: Temporal relations
docs.text: Story sequence is the order of sealed events. A causal edge must point from an earlier sealed event to a later one. A discourse act can reference any sealed story event and is itself ordered in the discourse stream. A later event's interpretation can target earlier story sequence numbers. The scrubber replays a prefix of story and optionally a prefix of discourse; this lets an author compare the world and the reader's disclosed information at a chosen point.

docs.title: Design invariants
docs.text:
• Exactly two fixture actors, with unique actor/entity IDs.
  • Event stream entries carry stable IDs and integrity hashes; earlier sealed entries are not edited in place.
  • Observation has an observer and an access path; belief revision cites evidence the observer could access.
  • Discourse reveal is grounded in referenced story facts, except when hypothetical/unreliable is explicitly marked.
  • Causal parents are earlier events; a draft causal graph cannot contain cycles.
  • Runs and exports are derived artifacts, separate from sealed canon.

docs.title: Run flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  V[Validate] --> R[Replay]
  R --> RV[Revise]
  RV --> P[Plan]
  P --> PK[Packet]
  PK --> Z[Realize]
  Z --> C[Check]
  C --> Saved[(Run JSON and packet JSON)]

These seven names are recorded in each run's stages. In this release, Project.run performs packet construction, deterministic realization, and checks synchronously; the stage entries are a report of that process, not seven independent worker services. If findings exist, the run marks an applicable stage failed and later stages skipped. The pipeline lens shows latest stage status for C0–C3.

docs.title: Packet content
docs.text: build_packet replays the branch and combines ordered discourse acts with referenced story payloads, grounded story facts, prose style, simulated reader state, forbidden assertions, unresolved questions, and word bounds. A canonical hash identifies the packet. The packet is saved at packets/<packet-hash>.json when running.

docs.title: Realization
docs.text: template_realize joins authored discourse text with blank lines. If an act has no text, it uses referenced story descriptions/titles. The unchanged seeded Mara and Len story can use authored expanded paragraphs; custom projects and edited cues use their actual authored text. No network or model API is used.

docs.title: Checks and limits
docs.text:
Check Current behavior Word bounds Counts word-like tokens and compares with contract min/max Forbidden assertions Case-insensitive literal substring search in realized prose Required story conditions Confirms each required condition occurs in grounded story facts Missing content Flags empty story or discourse Disclosure grounding Validated when sealing discourse acts

facts_that_must_be_clear, questions_that_must_remain_open, and strain_threshold_bp are stored contract fields but are not fully evaluated by the current run checker. There is no general semantic grounding proof, private-cognition leak detector, or model adapter. The manual explains how to read a finding.

docs.title: Current limits and roadmap
docs.text:
This page distinguishes the running app from the broader SRS-033 design. The detailed requirement and scenario checkpoint lives in _design/SRS-033-Implementation-Status.md.

Area Implemented now Planned in the source design Authoring Story/discourse drafts, preview, seal, fork, basic compare Full fixture/mind/rule palette editing and richer diff tools State Deterministic replay, six projections, basic revisions and formula preconditions Formal modal/conceptual revision operators and richer provenance Realization Offline authored text/template, packet and run hashes Model adapters, budget and cassette record/replay Checking Structural invariants, word bounds, literal forbidden strings Semantic grounding and private-knowledge leak detection Evaluation Individual Markdown run export Blinded sets, evaluator workflow, import, statistical analysis Recovery Persistent drafts, project lock, sidecar restart once Complete crash recovery and published-run replication

Scenario S-04's diagnostic flow is useful today, but a subtle claim can pass the basic checker. Scenarios S-07–S-12 specify research/evaluation or model service features that are not in this implementation. The user manual confines procedures to available actions and marks the limits at each relevant step.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
project.cmne.json
.cmne.lock
fixtures/active.json
contracts/active.json
branches/<branch-id>/story.ndjson
branches/<branch-id>/discourse.ndjson
branches/<branch-id>/evaluation.ndjson
drafts/<draft-id>.json
packets/<packet-hash>.json
runs/<run-id>.json
exports/<run-id>.md

The metadata file records the name, active branch, parent, fork sequence, and condition labels where present. Fixture and contract are current JSON documents with content hashes. Story and discourse streams contain one event per line. Drafts are mutable JSON; packets, runs, and exports are generated from sealed data.

docs.title: Event integrity
docs.text: An event contains stream, branch_id, one-based sequence, schema_version, payload, event_id, and integrity_hash. IDs and hashes come from canonical JSON with sorted keys and SHA-256. On read, the kernel verifies sequence, schema, ID, hash, and duplicate IDs. Stream writes replace a complete file atomically. A project lock prevents a second writer; normal close removes the lock. Never edit a sealed stream directly.

docs.title: Fork semantics
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  M[Main: S01 to S07] --> F[Fork at sequence 7]
  F --> A[Branch A: verified prefix plus new suffix]
  F --> B[Branch B: verified prefix plus new suffix]
  A --> RA[Run A]
  B --> RB[Run B]

Forking copies a verified story prefix and the initial contiguous discourse acts whose references remain in that prefix into a new branch. It stops copying discourse at the first act that refers beyond the prefix. The old story suffix becomes editable draft nodes on the new branch. When sealed, those nodes receive new event IDs. branch.compare reports common payload prefix, first divergence, counts unique to each branch, and projection hashes. It does not generate a prose diff.

docs.title: Reproducibility boundary
docs.text: Replay reduces fixture, contract, and selected event prefixes into six projections and content hashes. Integer basis points avoid floating-point state in strain and confidence fields. The run saves the packet hash, projection hashes, realizer ID, stages, prose, and findings. This supports local repeatability; published replication, adapter cassettes, and full evaluation provenance remain future work.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
Path Purpose mkdocs.yml Navigation, Material theme, Mermaid support, and build paths site/ Markdown source for the documentation doc/ Generated HTML output; ignored by Git

MkDocs normally uses docs/ as its input and site/ as its output. This project deliberately reverses those roles: docs_dir: site and site_dir: doc.

docs.title: Procedure: install and preview
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv                 # skip if it already exists
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[docs]'
mkdocs serve

Open the local URL printed by mkdocs serve. The docs extra installs Material for MkDocs 9.x. Mermaid diagrams use Material's native pymdownx.superfences configuration; write them as fenced mermaid blocks in Markdown.

docs.title: Procedure: build HTML
docs.text:
source .venv/bin/activate
mkdocs build --strict

Open doc/index.html or serve the doc/ directory with any static-file server. use_directory_urls: false gives pages explicit .html paths for local builds. --strict treats broken relative links and navigation problems as build failures.

docs.title: Principle: keep source and output separate
docs.text: Edit pages under site/, then rebuild. Do not edit generated files under doc/. The generated directory is ignored so changes to the manual remain reviewable as Markdown.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• MkDocs configuration describes docs_dir and site_dir.
  • Material for MkDocs diagrams describes the native Mermaid fence.

docs.title: Fact: supported local path
docs.text: The verified packaging path is an unsigned macOS app. It builds a React frontend, Rust Tauri shell, and PyInstaller Python sidecar. A current Python 3.11+, Node 22+ with npm, Rust 1.90+ with Cargo, and macOS Tauri prerequisites are required. The packaged app includes Python; the development app uses a local virtual environment.

docs.title: Procedure: install dependencies yourself
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[bundle]'
cd app
npm ci
cd ..

.[bundle] installs CMNE and PyInstaller into .venv. npm ci reads the committed app/package-lock.json. React and Tauri are built by the next command.

docs.title: Procedure: build and launch the packaged app
docs.text:
./build_app.sh --skip-install
./launch_app.sh

If dependencies are not installed yet, run ./build_app.sh without the flag. It creates .venv if needed and installs Python and Node dependencies before building. The output is app/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/CMNE Workbench.app. The launcher opens that bundle.

Rebuild after changing Python code

launch_app.sh opens the most recent bundle. After changing src/cmne/ or src/cmne_sidecar/, run ./build_app.sh --skip-install again. Quit a running copy of the app before relaunching it.

docs.title: Procedure: run from source
docs.text:
source .venv/bin/activate
cd app
npm run tauri -- dev

The Tauri development command prepares a sidecar wrapper and starts Vite. Return to the repository root before using commands shown elsewhere in this manual.

docs.title: Procedure: verify the installation
docs.text:
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
(cd app && npm run build)
(cd app/src-tauri && cargo check)

The tests cover selected kernel and sidecar behavior; they are not the complete target SRS acceptance suite. See current limits.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: At first launch, the app creates or opens ~/Documents/CMNE/Mara and Len. If it has already been opened, the app first tries the last project saved in browser-local state. The sample project's files stay on the local machine.

docs.title: User manual: work from a question
docs.text:
This manual starts with a task, shows the action, and then explains the construct behind it. Its structure adapts Robert E. Horn's Information Mapping approach: small, labeled units with one purpose and a presentation suited to the reader's question. The Information Mapping methodology identifies information units and types; its type guide distinguishes concept, structure, process, procedure, principle, and fact.

Label in this manual Reader question Typical form Concept What is it? Short definition and example Structure What parts does it have? Part/function table or diagram Process What happens? Stage/result table Procedure How do I do it? Numbered steps and expected result Principle What rule should guide my choice? Constraint and reason Fact What is true in this release? Specific behavior or limit

docs.title: Task map
docs.text:
Scenario Your question Page S-01 What does the sample do? First run S-02 How do I make my own scene? Build a scene S-03, S-05 How do I revise an interpretation or remove an event safely? Revise and compare S-04 Why did a run fail, and how do I get a passage? Generate and export S-06 What differs between C1 and C3? Read the result S-10, S-13 What happens when a process stops or a draft remains? Troubleshooting

The remaining design scenarios S-07–S-09, S-11, and S-12 describe blinded evaluation, adapter extension, and published-run replication. Those flows are not implemented in the current application; see roadmap.

docs.title: Principle: separate evidence from interpretation
docs.text: An event records what happened. An interpretation records an observer's reading of it, with a model version and possible references back to earlier events. A discourse act decides what the reader encounters and when. Keeping these distinct lets a later reinterpretation change Mara's understanding without rewriting Len's earlier repair.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Create a bounded local project, record what happens, decide what the reader sees, and seal a runnable scene. This procedure uses the current GUI. For advanced fixture, contract, and revision fields, use the JSON-RPC API.

docs.title: Fact: current editing surface
docs.text: The GUI can create a project and edit story and discourse drafts. New projects begin with two placeholder actors (actor_a, actor_b) and no entities. Fixture, Mind, and Motif are mostly inspection lenses today. The GUI does not yet provide a palette for adding actors, objects, rules, or full revision operators. Rename actors or add entities through fixture.save before writing events; see contracts.

docs.title: Procedure: create a project
docs.text:
1. Click the project name in the top bar and choose Create new.
  2. Enter an absolute folder path that does not already contain a CMNE project, and a project name.
  3. Click Create project. The new project opens in Story lens. If you keep the placeholder fixture, use actor_a and actor_b in actor fields.

Result. The folder has project.cmne.json, a fixture, a contract, and a main branch. The new default contract has no required story conditions and permits 0–1100 words.

docs.title: Structure: minimum authoring constructs
docs.text: Construct What it stores Authoring choice Fixture Two actors, entities, initial facts, style Choose the cast and objects before sealing events Contract Required/forbidden story claims, open questions, word bounds, strain threshold Decide what the passage must and must not assert Story event Title, kind, participants, observations, optional facts/revisions, strain Say what happened in story time Discourse act Mode, text, focalizer, story references, reveal/withhold Decide when and how the reader encounters an event Draft Editable nodes and edges Work before committing to canon Sealed event Validated event in the NDJSON stream Preserve the branch's history

docs.title: Procedure: add story events
docs.text:
1. Open Story and choose Add event. Select the draft node.
  2. In the inspector, enter a specific Title and Description. Choose an event kind: action, observation, utterance, recollection, decision, revision, or crisis.
  3. Enter actor IDs in Actors. For an observation, enter at least one Observed by ID and choose a perception, testimony, or memory access path. The sidecar rejects an observation without these fields.
  4. Set the strain slider if the event increases or eases pressure. The stored value is an integer from 0 to 10,000 basis points; the UI displays a percentage.
  5. To record causation, select a draft event, click Connect from, then select the target story event. The sidecar checks the connection; a sealed event cannot gain a new causal parent.
  6. Repeat for each beat. Click Seal draft. Correct any field or connection errors reported by the preview, then seal again.

Result. The event or group of draft events is appended to the branch's story stream. Sealed events cannot be edited in place; fork to revise.

docs.title: Procedure: plan discourse
docs.text:
1. Open Discourse and choose Add act. Select the new draft act.
  2. Choose a mode such as scene, summary, memory, or pause. Enter Passage text and select a focalizer or narrator.
  3. Select the act and click Connect from, then select the story event it discloses. This creates a refs edge from the act to the event.
  4. If you use Reveal claims, each claim must match a world_facts value on a referenced story event. The GUI does not expose world_facts editing yet, so leave Reveal empty when using the GUI alone. A claim already revealed cannot later be withheld.
  5. Seal the discourse draft. Add more acts in the order the reader should encounter them, which may differ from story order.

Result. A run can produce prose from the acts' text. For custom projects, the offline realizer joins the authored act text in discourse order; it does not invent missing scenes. Set enough text to satisfy your contract's word bounds.

docs.title: Principle: keep private knowledge out of observed events
docs.text: An observation must name who had access and how. This is a narrow validation rule in the current release. The prose checker does not yet reliably detect every sentence that implies another character's private thought. Write and review the passage accordingly.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Generate and export the passage, then read its findings.

docs.title: Concept — the narrative layers
docs.text: Layer Meaning Sample example Fixture Stable cast, objects, starting facts, style Mara, Len, chair, bowl Contract Conditions and limits for a run Keep a question open; prose word bounds Story Events in causal/chronological sequence Chair rocks; Mara sees a note Discourse Order and manner of telling A later paragraph remembers the chair Projection Derived state after replay Mara's belief, reader disclosure, strain Packet Bounded input to the realizer Ordered acts, grounded facts, limits Run Saved prose and findings A C3 passage and its Check status

docs.title: Structure — story event
docs.text:
A story event has a title and a kind (action, observation, utterance, recollection, decision, revision, or crisis). Optional fields include description, actor/entity IDs, earlier causal parents, world facts, observers, interpretations, revisions, and strain_bp.

For an observation, identify an observer and access_path: perception, testimony, or memory. For a belief revision, point to an earlier event the observer actually observed. A causal parent must already be sealed on that branch.

docs.title: Structure — discourse act
docs.text: A discourse act has a title and a mode: scene, summary, ellipsis, pause, memory, or repetition. story_refs link it to sealed story events. text is its authored narration; focalizer selects a known actor. reveal must be grounded in the referenced events' world facts unless the act is marked hypothetical or unreliable. withhold cannot name a claim already revealed in a previous act.

docs.title: Process — how interpretations change the past
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[Earlier sealed event] --> B[Later observation]
  B --> C[Later interpretation targets earlier sequence]
  C --> D[Replay updates actor projection]
  A --> E[Original event stays sealed]

An interpretation records an observer, claim, positive model version, and optional earlier target sequences. It changes the derived mind projection. It does not alter the referenced event. A belief revision records accepted, rejected, or suspended status and confidence in basis points. A modal revision adds possible scenarios; a conceptual revision creates a new model version and migration map. These implemented transitions are basic representations of the richer theory in Domain model.

docs.title: Principle — authoring boundaries
docs.text: Edit Story and Discourse through drafts, then preview and seal. Once sealed, fork to change a story suffix. The other five lenses are read-only views of fixture or derived state. Fixture and contract JSON can be managed through the sidecar API; the current GUI has no direct editors for them.

docs.title: Fact — formula language
docs.text: Preconditions use JSON AST operators atom, not, and, or, implies, necessarily, possibly, believes, suspends, and in_scenario. Evaluation can return true, false, or unknown. The validator limits depth to 16 and nodes to 256. See Data contracts.

docs.title: S-01 · See Mara and Len run
Concept: the bounded experiment
docs.text:
Mara tries to understand Len's leaving. A repaired chair, a blue bowl, and a note become evidence that can be read in more than one way. The sample contains story events S01–S10 and discourse acts D01–D07. Four branches share S01–S07 and diverge at the interpretation of what Mara has learned.

Condition Change represented in the sample Question to ask while reading C0 A new external fact What does the address settle, and what does it leave open? C1 A belief is rejected Which inference does Mara stop making? C2 Another possibility becomes admissible Can care and departure coexist? C3 A concept divides and remains unresolved Do the chair and bowl change meaning without changing as facts?

These are experimental design conditions, not evidence that one passage is better literature. The present offline sample uses authored prose; it does not call a model.

docs.title: Procedure: run the sample
docs.text:
1. Launch the app. The first launch opens Mara and Len · The chair and the bowl. If another project opens, choose the project name at the top and select Open bundled Mara and Len sample.
  2. In the Story lens, select the chair repair, departure, note, and crisis events. The inspector shows each event's canonical fields.
  3. Click Run C0–C3. The run is synchronous; wait for the result. The Pipeline lens then shows seven recorded stages for each condition.
  4. Choose a C3 branch in the left sidebar. In Latest Run, open Read generated passage. Read the final paragraphs about the chair and bowl.
  5. Switch to C1 and read its passage. Use Compare branches for the shared prefix and first diverging sequence.

Result. Each seeded condition yields a deterministic passage of roughly 800 words and a saved run. A previous short run record remains until you run again after installing an updated build.

docs.title: Structure: seven lenses
docs.text: Lens Main question Current use Fixture Who and what are present? Inspect actors and objects Story What happened? Draft, seal, fork, inspect causal and retrospective edges Discourse In what order is it told? Draft telling acts and connect them to story events Mind What does an actor believe or consider possible? Inspect basic belief, scenario, model, and interpretation nodes Provenance Which event supports a claim? Inspect a basic evidence/claim graph Motif Where do marked objects recur? Inspect basic appearances of the chair and bowl Pipeline What did a run record? Inspect completed stage status per condition

docs.title: Process: story versus telling
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph StoryTime[Story order]
      S1[S01 Chair repaired] --> S5[S05 Len leaves] --> S7[S07 Note names dates] --> S9[S09 Mara revises]
    end
    subgraph TellingOrder[Discourse order]
      D1[D01 Rocking chair] --> D2[D02 Ordinary reason] --> D3[D03 Note found] --> D4[D04 Chair remembered] --> D6[D06 Meanings held]
    end
    D4 -. refers to .-> S1
    D1 -. refers to .-> S5
    D6 -. refers to .-> S9

The chart shows why the reader can meet the effect before learning the cause. Domain model and theory explains the distinction in more detail.

docs.title: Generate and export a passage — S-04
Concept — generation in this release
docs.text: A run reads the selected branch's sealed story and discourse, builds a scene packet, assembles prose with the offline deterministic realizer, and checks the result. It does not call a language model. A run saves its result separately from the sealed events; running again does not edit canon.

docs.title: Process — from plan to report
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[Sealed story and discourse] --> B[Scene packet]
  B --> C[Offline realization]
  C --> D[Word and forbidden-text checks]
  D --> E[Saved run JSON]
  E --> F[Markdown export]

docs.title: Procedure — generate the sample
docs.text:
1. Open Mara and Len and select a C0–C3 branch.
  2. Select Run for that branch, or Run C0–C3 for all four sample conditions.
  3. Read the passage and run status in the passage/pipeline views. For all four, select each branch to inspect its own passage.
  4. If the status is failed, read the finding and correct the named story, discourse, or contract issue. Fork first if the correction changes a sealed event.
  5. Run again. The newest run is the one used by export for the selected branch.

docs.title: Procedure — export the story
docs.text:
1. Select the branch whose passage you want.
  2. Run that branch at least once.
  3. Choose Export report in the workbench.
  4. Open the returned Markdown file at <project>/exports/<run-id>.md in any text or Markdown editor. The report contains the project title, run ID, status, passage, and findings.

The export is a Markdown report. For a plain story, copy the text under Passage. The run's complete machine-readable record remains at <project>/runs/<run-id>.json.

docs.title: Procedure — generate from the command line
docs.text:
source .venv/bin/activate
cmne run "/path/to/project" --branch main

The CLI prints run JSON, including prose, status, and findings. It does not create the Markdown report; use the desktop Export report action or the sidecar's export.report.

docs.title: Principle — writing a custom scene
docs.text: For a new project, the realizer joins nonempty discourse text in discourse order, separated by blank lines. If an act has no text, it falls back to the descriptions or titles of its referenced story events. Write the desired narration in the discourse acts and use story_refs to keep each act tied to sealed events. The 700–1,100-word authored expansion belongs only to the unchanged Mara and Len seed; an edited cue or a new project uses its own text.

docs.title: Fact — what the checker tests
docs.text: The implemented checker tests word bounds and literal forbidden assertions, plus run-level missing story/discourse and required story facts. It does not prove every sentence true or detect all leaked private knowledge. Read the passage yourself for voice, continuity, and grounding. See Read the result.

docs.title: Concept — four different outputs
docs.text: Output What it answers Where to find it Passage What does the reader see? Passage view; prose in run JSON; exported report Findings and stages Did the current checks pass? Pipeline view; findings, stages, and status in run JSON Projection What does the engine derive at this point? Mind, Provenance, Motif, strain views; scrubber; scrub.projection Trace What supports this selected story event? Trace details; trace.query

docs.title: Procedure — read the sample output
docs.text:
1. Select C0 and read the passage in discourse order. Notice how the chair and bowl recur while the ending leaves the central question open.
  2. Select C1, C2, then C3. Compare the interpretation of earlier events, not only the final action. C1 changes a belief, C2 adds a possible scenario, and C3 changes the categories Mara uses.
  3. In Story, inspect the causal chain and strain values. In Discourse, inspect which story event each act references, what it reveals, and what it withholds.
  4. Scrub to an earlier story sequence and compare the actor and reader projections with the final state. Discourse can point back to an earlier event; telling order is independent of story order.
  5. Open Trace on a story event. Read its causal parents, observers, disclosures, and later interpretations. A later interpretation may target an earlier sequence without rewriting that event.
  6. Check Pipeline and the findings list. passed means the implemented checks found no violation; it is not a literary quality score.

docs.title: Structure — run JSON
docs.text:
{
  "run_id": "run_…",
  "branch_id": "branch_…",
  "conditions": ["C3"],
  "packet_hash": "…",
  "prose": "The passage…",
  "findings": [],
  "stages": [{"condition": "C3", "stage": "Check", "status": "passed"}],
  "projection_hashes": {"actor_a": "…", "reader": "…"},
  "status": "passed",
  "realizer": "deterministic-template-v2"
}

The actual run also contains run_sequence and all seven stage entries. Hashes identify packet and projection content; they are useful for comparing repeatable runs, not for interpreting the prose.

docs.title: Principle — a finding is a diagnostic
docs.text: E-PROSE-WORDS means the generated word count is outside the contract's bounds. E-PROSE-FORBIDDEN means a forbidden string appears in the prose. E-RUN-CONTRACT means a required story condition is absent from the grounded story facts. E-RUN-EMPTY and E-RUN-PLAN mean story or discourse is missing. A failed stage indicates the layer where the current implementation classifies the problem. Troubleshooting gives recovery steps.

docs.title: Fact — what the strain chart shows
docs.text: strain_bp is an author supplied value from 0 to 10,000 at each story event. The chart plots that sequence; it is not a measurement of reader emotion. The current telling tension projection is a simple function of the number of withheld claims. Use these numbers to inspect your own design choices, not as an external evaluation.

docs.title: S-03, S-05, S-06 · Revise and compare
Concept: three levels of revision
docs.text:
The Mara/Len conditions isolate different changes. Belief revision changes the status of one claim; modal revision adds a possible scenario; conceptual revision changes the model's vocabulary or interpretation map. The current kernel implements basic transitions for all three, but the full formal operators and revision planner in the target design are not built.

Condition In the sample What remains unchanged C1 belief Mara rejects “The repairs are care.” Earlier chair and bowl events C2 modal Mara admits “care and departure coexist” as a scenario. Earlier facts and their event IDs C3 conceptual Mara's model moves to v2; care maps to care and avoidance, with unresolved terms. Earlier story events; new interpretation records point back to S01 and S02

docs.title: Procedure: fork a sealed event
docs.text:
1. In Story, select the sealed event where the alternative should begin.
  2. Click Fork from here and name the branch. The new branch keeps the sealed prefix before that event and opens draft copies of the selected event and its suffix.
  3. Edit the draft copies in the inspector, add or remove draft nodes, and check their causal connections.
  4. Click Seal draft. The source branch remains intact; the new branch gets its own suffix.
  5. Run the new branch and compare it with the source branch.

Result. The branch comparer reports shared prefix length, first diverging sequence, suffix counts, and projection hashes. It does not yet show the designed graph diff overlay.

docs.title: Process: safe alternative history
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    P[S01–S07 shared sealed prefix] --> A[S08–S10 original branch]
    P --> B[Editable suffix draft]
    B --> C[Validate and seal new branch]
    A --> D[Compare projections]
    C --> D

S-05 example. To ask whether the chair's rocking matters, select the event where it appears, fork, remove its draft copy, and repair later references or preconditions before sealing. The old branch remains available for comparison. The current editor does not provide a one-click visual diff.

docs.title: Procedure: compare C1 and C3
docs.text:
1. Run C0–C3 from the seeded sample.
  2. Select C1 in the left branch list. Click Compare branches and choose C3.
  3. Read the shared prefix and first difference in the comparison panel.
  4. Switch between branches in Mind and Story. On C3, inspect the model v2 node and the retrospective links to S01/S02. In C1, inspect the rejected belief.
  5. Read each passage and note what changed for the character, then what changed for the reader. Read the result explains the limits of that comparison.

docs.title: Principle: an interpretation is not a new fact
docs.text: Mara can reinterpret the chair repair under model v2 while S01 still says the same thing happened. A different interpretation may change the significance of an event without editing the event's canon. Keep that distinction when writing the prose and when comparing conditions.

docs.title: Fact: sample prose on edited branches
docs.text: The long authored expansion is used only when the Mara/Len fixture and story still match a seeded condition and its discourse cues are unchanged. If canon changes, the offline realizer uses the branch's authored discourse text. This prevents the seed's prepared prose from describing a different event as if it were still true.

docs.title: Procedure — a run failed
docs.text:
1. Read the finding code and message in the run view or saved runs/<run-id>.json.
  2. For E-RUN-EMPTY, seal a story event. For E-RUN-PLAN, seal a discourse act that references story.
  3. For E-RUN-CONTRACT, add the required world fact to a story event, or correct the contract if the requirement was wrong.
  4. For E-PROSE-WORDS, edit the discourse text or the contract bounds. For E-PROSE-FORBIDDEN, revise the authored text and run again.
  5. If the correction changes a sealed event, fork before editing. Export the new run after it passes.

docs.title: Procedure — a draft did not seal
docs.text:
1. Keep the draft open and run its preview validation.
  2. Follow the error's field_path: check title, actor IDs, story references, causal edges, observation access, and disclosure grounding.
  3. Correct the draft and preview again. A rejected seal returns errors and does not emit events.
  4. Seal after preview accepts it. Draft JSON persists in <project>/drafts/ until sealed or deleted; after an interrupted session, reopen the project and inspect the recovered draft.

docs.title: Principle — preserve project integrity
docs.text: Do not hand edit sealed NDJSON streams. The engine verifies event IDs, hashes, sequence, and schema when reading them. A second writer receives E-LOCK-001; close the first app/process before reopening the project. Back up the whole project directory when sharing or archiving a branch.

docs.title: Fact — current recovery scope
docs.text: The shell can restart a failed sidecar once; saved drafts and sealed streams survive a normal process interruption. There is no model service or cost budget in the current release, so the model outage flow from scenario S-10 is a future feature. run.cancel reports that no asynchronous run is active; a run is synchronous. The roadmap identifies further recovery work.
